---
title: "Research"
---

My research asks how aquatic vegetation and restoration interventions shape freshwater and
coastal ecosystems — and what that means for carbon, biodiversity and the people managing
these systems. Below are the projects I lead or contribute to.

## RESTORE4Cs {#restore4cs}

_Horizon Europe · 2023–_

Assessing the role of coastal wetland restoration in climate mitigation. I led the writing of
the project's state-of-the-art deliverable on coastal wetland restoration, and I coordinate
several large-scale meta-analyses on how restoration affects carbon cycling and biodiversity.
On the field side, I coordinated and conducted a 24-week sampling campaign across six European
countries, covering field planning, protocol design and data collection.

Three meta-analyses are currently running with a team of over 30 researchers, covering
greenhouse gas pathways, wetland-type-specific emission responses, and biodiversity outcomes.
The first is available as a preprint:
[Coastal wetland restoration and greenhouse gas pathways](https://doi.org/10.31223/x51b39).

## EUPHORIA {#euphoria}

_European Federation of Freshwater Sciences FreshProject · PI · 2025–_

EUPHORIA studies macrophyte phenology across a European climatic gradient. As principal
investigator I coordinate more than 110 early-career researchers from 22 countries — project
design, standardised field protocols, participant training, team formation, finances and
workshops. The project also develops citizen science initiatives around aquatic plant
monitoring.

Funded as the 5th Collaborative European Freshwater Science Project for Young Researchers.

## Macrophyte management and aquatic biodiversity

_PhD, Université de Rennes 1 · 2019–2023_

My doctoral work asked what happens to aquatic communities when macrophytes are removed —
a common management response to mass plant development. Working across sites in Europe and
South Africa, I combined multinational field surveys with mesocosm experiments to track
responses in phytoplankton, zooplankton and macroinvertebrates, and contributed to
assessments of carbon fluxes, ecosystem services and willingness-to-pay for removal.

The short-term biodiversity results are published in _Journal of Environmental Management_;
the long-term analysis is in preparation.

## Collaborative projects

**Global Littoral Zone GHG Flux Database** (2025–) — contributing to a global sampling campaign
on methane and CO₂ fluxes from macrophyte-dominated littoral zones, feeding an open-access
database and a collaborative publication.

**EFS Macrophyte Life Form Dataset** (2024–) — species-level trait data on morphology and
functional structure for a global standardised dataset of aquatic plant life forms.

**PhytoPlastic** (2022–) — algal colonisation of plastics in aquatic systems; data management,
analysis and outreach.

**EUROPONDS** (2020–) — emerging insects from ponds across Europe; co-lead on collaborative
manuscript writing, plus data management and outreach.

## Earlier work

**Flow intermittency in alpine streams** — as a research assistant at Eawag on the InterNet
project, I worked on experimental manipulation of flow intermittency in the Val Roseg,
Switzerland, covering fieldwork, macroinvertebrate identification and stable isotope sample
preparation. This continued from my MSc at ETH Zürich on flow intermittency and biodiversity
in an alpine fluvial network.

**Alpine springs under climatic stress** — my BSc at the University of Basel examined how water
temperature shapes species assemblages in alpine springs in the Bernese Alps.
